result_text:
The `mock` scoping rule now matches any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock`, whatever follows. The new tests pass.

**Change:** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, `addTestConventions`, I replaced the two folder rules:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` → `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` → `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

The `[^/]*` lets the name be empty or contain any character except a path separator, so the match stays inside one folder. Backslash paths already work because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` also tries a `\`→`/` replacement. `mockapi/`, `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/` and the `_mock.ext` file rule are unchanged, so they still match.

**Tests:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It covers the three newly caught kinds (`mock`, `mock.data`/`mock(old)`, `mock-größe`/`mock模拟`), the backslash form, the previously matched folders, and the negative cases (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`). It and `SourceFileFilterTest` pass (`mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test`; 2 and 6 tests, no failures).

Nothing is committed.
